newsitem.title: UK: Dlr powers to new 4-yr peak above 125 yen in Europ.
newsitem.headline: Dlr powers to new 4-yr peak above 125 yen in Europ.

text.p: The dollar powered to its highest level in four years on Monday, ripping through 125 yen in Europe as yield differentials between the world's key economies and the start of Japan's fiscal year boosted demand for the U.S. unit.
"What is driving the market at the moment are (these) dual considerations," said Julian Fisher, economist at Daiwa Europe.

Fisher said with the end-of-year repatriation of Japanese assets over, the focus has now shifted to the potential for Japanese assets to be diversified as the 1997/98 fiscal year begins and investors bank on fresh U.S. interest rate rises.
"It seems fairly plain that there will be at least one more rise in U.S. interest rates at a time when real rates in Japan are set to turn negative," said Daiwa's Fisher.

U.S. interest rates, which rose on March 25 for the first time in two years, have already increased the pull on Japan's cash and analysts said expectations for even higher rates after healthy jobless figures on Friday will contrast with yields in Japan where interest rates are among the world's lowest.
Dollar bulls, said analysts, were also encouraged on Monday by the lack of trade friction caused by U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin's visit to Japan and his stance on the dollar.
Analysts said the market failed to react to Rubin when he urged Japan to guard against a resurgence in its trade surplus and warned a further rise would re-ignite trade friction.
"The market was geared up for Rubin to talk a bit tougher on trade policy," said Nick Parsons, foreign exchange strategist at Banque Paribas.

Speaking in Hanoi, Rubin reiterated the dollar has been strong for "quite some time" and this has been helpful to the U.S. economy. "I think that the strength of the dollar that we've had for quite some time now has spurred low interest rates, low rates of inflation...in the United States," he said.
"Having said that, I am not expressing any view...with regard to the level or direction that we would seek one way or another," he added.
The Japan-U.S. surplus had had the market wary of verbal intervention by Rubin to stem dollar strength.

Japan's current account surplus rose in February for the second month in a row, though dollar markets shrugged it off and instead moved higher. Tokyo's surplus in its current account, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, rose 15.4 percent to 865.2 billion yen ($6.92 billion) in February from a year earlier, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) announced on Monday.
The surplus was slightly above economists' average forecast of 801.1 billion yen ($6.40 billion) and follows a rise in January, the first in 17 months.
At 1055 GMT the dollar stood at 125.30/5.35 yen and just off fresh four-year peaks of 125.38 yen touched in Europe, and over one-yen up from 124.20/30 in late Europe on Friday.
The dollar also sprinted higher against the mark and at midday in Europe stood at 1.7006/16 marks, just below near three-week peaks of 1.7033 marks touched earlier.
Analysts said the dollar got a leg-up against the mark as the odds in favour of European Monetary Union increased.
